candidates.answer: The Hall-deficiency certificate is sound: if a witness set S has a neighborhood union smaller than |S|, no injective transversal exists. Proof by counting: an injective transversal's image lies in the neighborhood union and has cardinality |S|, contradicting |neighborhood union| < |S|.
candidates.falsification: a counterexample to the stated theorem

root.statement: For any neighborhood map t : iota -> Finset alpha and any witness set S : Finset iota, if S is deficient (the union of neighborhoods of S is strictly smaller than S), then there is no injective transversal of S into its neighborhoods. This is the soundness core of the Hall-deficiency argument: a deficient witness blocks every matching.
